messages.author: 794570edb1de2b89
messages.subject: CentOS vs Ubuntu
parts: We currently have a Shiny Server running in CentOS 6.9. I noticed that shinyapps.io seems to run in a Debian OS (Ubuntu?). I was wondering and I guess this is not necessarily a Shiny only question but an R question. I would think that Ubuntu is preferred because some R packages may require later system dependencies. Any experiences? Would you go with Ubuntu? CentOS? Which one would require the least amount of installing libraries from source? I realize this is a general question but I was wondering if anybody have experience running the Shiny Server in multiple systems and if you can provide any feedback.

messages.author: 6ca62a5f409b469f
messages.subject: Re: CentOS vs Ubuntu
parts:
Hi,
Ubuntu is probably more widely used than CentOS, and so the principal advantage I see of running it would just be that more people are running into and fixing more kinds of problems on it than any other distro. In my experience this makes problems easier to Google for, and to find solutions to various R-on-Linux problems.

At least, that's been the reason I've tended to use Debian-based/Ubuntu OSes and continue to. OTOH, I've never worked around people with deep CentOS knowledge. If I did, I might find their ability to help me more valuable than Googling. My .02.

Alan

messages.author: 5ab11db47365dff1
messages.subject: Re: CentOS vs Ubuntu
parts:
CentOS is an OS designed to be "safe" and secure and stable for a long time. They are slower to update packages and have longer release cycles. Ubuntu released more quickly, has LTS versions every couple of years, and keeps packages more on the bleeding edge.

This means, for example, that without any tinkering you're going to get a newer default version of R out of the box on ubuntu than CentOS.

Use CentOS if

1. You like and are comfortable with it.
2.  You're working with a team of people who are familiar with the Red Hat ecosystem, and therefore they are more comfortable with CentOS
3.  You have some other apps that require CentOS


Otherwise, I'd just go with Ubuntu.  I think you'll find things will be easier as its more popular and had a wider user base and updates more frequently.

Erik
